column1: ## THE APP-PAGE CENSUS LIST — JS-heavy application pages, the corpus §What-the-tool-produces names ("target
## JS-heavy app/feature pages, not marketing pages"). It is a SECOND list beside sites.tsv, not a replacement:
## sites.tsv is LOGIN pages and this is APP pages, and the two answer different questions about the same
## engine. Neither header states its own length: a count in prose is the one field here that goes stale the
## moment a row is appended, and the rows below are the only place that can answer it.
## IT IS CHECKED IN BECAUSE THE MEASUREMENT IT NAMES WAS NOT. The census that produced this project's
## standing headline — ten of twelve ENGINE-ABORT, `fin/n` 0 everywhere, `sinks: 0` on every measurable
## site — was driven from a list and a driver that existed only under /tmp, so the one artifact needed to
## re-measure it was the one artifact the checkout did not have. A number nobody can re-measure is not a
## baseline, it is an anecdote, and CLAUDE.md §Testing's whole demand (report a live number with its run
## count and its spread) presupposes somebody can run it again.
## THE THIRD COLUMN IS AN OBSERVATION, NOT A LABEL. It records what the SHIPPED DOCUMENT says about its own
## bundler — the script names and module attributes actually present in the bytes this list's URLs served —
## because a stack named from recollection is the citation-without-a-number defect wearing a build tool's
## name. A page whose document names nothing says so.
## THIS LIST ONLY GROWS, AND A DEAD ENTRY KEEPS ITS ROW. Two of the original twelve serve HTTP 403 to this
## environment and always have, so every census run against this list measured TEN sites under a twelve-site
## name — and the report's `measurable` column is the only place that said so. The reflex is to delete them,
## and it is wrong twice: report.mjs is FATAL on a census row its list does not name (a row the list does not
## contain is a claim about a corpus nobody selected), so deleting a row makes every historical census file
## unreadable; and the 403 is itself an observation worth keeping, because a site that blocks this environment
## is a fact about what this corpus can reach, not an absence. So a blocked entry stays, its third column
## records the status it actually returns, and a replacement is APPENDED beside it.
## Lines beginning `#` are comments. Columns: id, url, observed stack.
## THE FIRST TWELVE ROWS WERE SELECTED ON BUNDLER DIVERSITY, AND THAT AXIS CANNOT MEASURE THE @H HALF. A
## census of them reported 67 endpoints across the corpus and every one of them was an IMAGE: squoosh's nine
## were the document's nine `` values one-to-one in markup order, and figma's fifty-four were 21
## `data:` URLs and 33 files from a CMS image CDN. Not one API endpoint has ever been learned from this list.
## That is not the engine failing the corpus; it is the corpus never having asked the engine the question,
## because a page with no backend has no API surface to find and three of these pages are in-browser editors.
## So a row is selected on FIVE tests, and the third column records the bytes each one was decided on:
##   1. A REACHABLE SAME-ORIGIN BACKEND SERVING JSON, proven by an anonymous request that returned one — never
##      by a path found in a bundle, which proves only that somebody wrote the string.
##   2. SURFACE BEHIND STATE THE BUNDLE SHIPS AND DOES NOT RUN. This is the project's actual proposition
##      (§What-the-tool-produces: "learn the LOGGED-IN API surface WHILE LOGGED OUT"), so it is the one test a
##      corpus cannot omit and still be measuring this tool. It is proven the same way: a route the shipped
##      bundle names, requested anonymously, answering 401/403/303 beside a sibling that answers 200.
##   3. SURVIVES A HEADLESS LOAD WITHOUT AUTH — a real app document, not an SSO wall and not a 403 shell.
##   4. MIRRORABLE, so a before/after is on FROZEN BYTES (§Testing). The test is mechanical: does `mirror.mjs`
##      reach the app's JavaScript, which it does through `<script src>` and `<link rel=preload/modulepreload
##      as=script>`? A page whose bundle is reached only by RUNNING its inline bootstrap fails this — the
##      engine can drive it live, and a number from it may never be quoted as a frozen-bytes comparison.
##   5. THE BUNDLER STACK IS AN OBSERVATION RECORDED AFTERWARDS, NEVER A SELECTION CRITERION.
## A VERDICT IN THE THIRD COLUMN IS A MEASUREMENT AND ITS ABSENCE IS "NOT ASSESSED", NEVER "PASSES". Most of
## the first twelve rows carry no verdict because nobody has fetched the bytes to give them one, and writing
## one from the shape of the site is the recollection-instead-of-citation defect this file's own header names.
## The rows that do carry one were probed: the status codes and byte counts in them are responses that
## actually came back. Sites change, so an observation is of the bytes served when it was written —
## `mirror.mjs`'s provenance.json holds the (url, date, sha256) triple that makes any of them re-checkable.
## A ROW IS NEVER DELETED, ONLY CORRECTED. `report.mjs` is fatal on a census row its list does not name, so a
## deleted id makes every historical census unreadable; a row that fails re-selection says so and stays.
squoosh

column3: PASSES 1-3, FAILS 4 — DRIVE LIVE, NEVER QUOTE AS A FROZEN-BYTES BEFORE/AFTER. /api/search?limit=2 returns 200 application/json 872B anonymously while /api/user returns 401 application/json (1 and 2, proven live), and the document carries a large inline window.grafanaBootData — server-injected absent state, which §Attacker-sources requires to stay symbolic and fork to the logged-in arm. It fails the mirror test because mirror.mjs reaches app JavaScript through <script src> and preload links and this document has neither, so it cannot be frozen until the mirror can follow a bootstrap that builds its own script tags. STACK: NO <script src> and NO preload link in the 16.8KiB document — four inline <script nonce> blocks build the app's script elements at runtime from grafana-assets.grafana.net
